key_insight: A fixed multi-layer quantum extreme learning machine can generate distributions and handwritten digits by training only a linear readout, but shows no advantage over matched classical random Fourier features at the studied sizes.
engineering_relevance: Keeping quantum dynamics fixed avoids quantum-circuit optimization and gradients through the device, simplifying training while retaining quantum measurement requirements.
method: Encode a scalar latent variable into a fixed, randomly initialized multi-layer quantum reservoir and measure expectation values.
Train a linear readout by minimizing maximum mean discrepancy between generated and target samples.
Encode class labels on dedicated qubits for conditional generation with a shared readout.
evidence_signal: Evaluations cover one- and two-dimensional distributions and six-qubit generation of Digits and MNIST images; physical Hamiltonian dynamics preserve performance when they spread inputs across the register.
watch_item: Quantum advantage is not demonstrated: a same-size classical random Fourier feature model performs equally well in the reported evaluations.
paper_title: Generative Models using Multi-layer Quantum Extreme Learning Machines
